subject: Chemistry
question: Which state of matter consists of a superheated gas composed of free electrons and positively charged ions capable of conducting electricity?

options.A: Plasma
options.C: Amorphous Solid

explanation: Plasma is the fourth state of matter, formed when thermal energy strips electrons from gaseous atoms, creating an ionized fluid of cations and electrons.

subject: Chemistry
question: What type of substance is formed when two or more elements chemically combine in a fixed ratio by mass?

options.A: Compound
options.C: Colloid

explanation: A chemical compound consists of atoms of two or more elements joined by chemical bonds in definite, fixed stoichiometric proportions (Law of Definite Proportions).

subject: Chemistry
question: Brass is an example of a solid-in-solid homogeneous solution composed primarily of:

options.A: Copper ($\text{Cu}$) and Zinc ($\text{Zn}$)
options.C: Iron ($\text{Fe}$) and Carbon ($\text{C}$)

explanation: Brass is an alloy (solid solution) made of copper and zinc, whereas bronze is made of copper and tin.

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following processes represents an irreversible chemical change rather than a physical phase transition?

options.A: The rusting of an iron nail in the presence of damp air
options.B: The sublimation of solid Iodine crystals upon gentle heating
options.C: The condensation of water vapor onto a cold glass surface
options.D: The dissolution of table salt in pure liquid water

explanation: Rusting creates a brand new chemical substance (hydrated iron(III) oxide, $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 \cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$) via redox reactions, whereas sublimation, condensation, and dissolution are reversible physical changes.

subject: Chemistry
question: According to the Kinetic Molecular Theory of matter, what happens to the average kinetic energy of gas molecules when the absolute temperature ($T$ in Kelvin) is doubled?

options.A: It doubles proportionally
options.C: It remains completely unchanged

explanation: The average kinetic energy of gas particles is directly proportional to the absolute thermodynamic temperature in Kelvin ($KE_{\text{avg}} \propto T$).

subject: Chemistry
question: Diamond and Graphite are allotropes of carbon. They have different physical properties because:

options.A: They possess different geometric arrangements and bonding patterns of carbon atoms in their crystal lattices
options.B: Diamond contains carbon-12 while graphite contains carbon-14
options.C: Diamond is an inorganic compound while graphite is an organic polymer
options.D: Graphite has ionic bonds while diamond has covalent bonds

explanation: Allotropy is the existence of an element in two or more physical forms due to differences in atomic arrangement and structural bonding (tetrahedral $sp^3$ network in diamond vs planar hexagonal $sp^2$ sheets in graphite).

subject: Chemistry
question: A mixture in which solute particles are large enough (greater than $1000\text{ nm}$) to settle out upon standing under gravity is classified as a:

options.A: Suspension
options.C: Colloid

explanation: In a suspension (like muddy water or milk of magnesia), particles are visible and precipitate over time under gravitational force.

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following optical phenomena allows one to distinguish a true solution from a colloidal dispersion?

options.A: Scattering of a visible light beam (Tyndall Effect)
options.B: Total internal reflection of radio waves
options.C: Nuclear magnetic resonance splitting

explanation: Colloidal particles are large enough ($1$ to $1000\text{ nm}$) to scatter a beam of light passing through the fluid (the Tyndall effect), making the path of light visible.

subject: Chemistry
question: According to Graham's law, which of the following gases will diffuse most rapidly at standard temperature and pressure ($STP$)?

options.A: Hydrogen gas ($\text{H}_2, M = 2\text{ g/mol}$)
options.C: Oxygen gas ($\text{O}_2, M = 32\text{ g/mol}$)

explanation: Rate of diffusion is inversely proportional to the square root of the molar mass ($r \propto 1/\sqrt{M}$). Since $\text{H}_2$ has the lowest molar mass ($2\text{ g/mol}$), it diffuses the fastest.

subject: Chemistry
question: The constant temperature at which a pure crystalline solid changes into a liquid at standard atmospheric pressure is called its:

options.A: Melting point
options.C: Boiling point

explanation: The melting point is the specific temperature at which the solid and liquid phases of a pure substance coexist in equilibrium at 1 atm.

subject: Chemistry
question: According to Graham's Law of diffusion, why does Ammonia gas ($\text{NH}_3, M = 17\text{ g/mol}$) diffuse faster than Hydrogen Chloride gas ($\text{HCl}, M = 36.5\text{ g/mol}$) at the same temperature?

options.A: Gases with lower molar mass possess higher average molecular speeds at a given kinetic energy ($r \propto 1/\sqrt{M}$)
options.B: Ammonia molecules have four times the mass of hydrogen chloride
options.C: Hydrogen chloride gas has no molecular mass
options.D: Ammonia gas is completely non-polar while HCl is metallic

explanation: Rate of diffusion is inversely proportional to the square root of molecular mass ($r_1/r_2 = \sqrt{M_2/M_1}$). Since $\text{NH}_3$ is lighter ($17 < 36.5$), its particles travel at higher velocity.

subject: Chemistry
question: During the boiling of pure liquid water at $100^\circ\text{C}$ under $1\text{ atm}$, the temperature remains constant despite continuous heating because added thermal energy is consumed as:

options.A: Latent Heat of Vaporization to overcome intermolecular hydrogen bonds between liquid water molecules
options.B: Energy to split water into elemental hydrogen and oxygen gases
options.C: Nuclear binding energy inside oxygen nuclei
options.D: Heat absorbed by the glass thermometer

explanation: During a phase transition from liquid to vapor, heat supplied is utilized as latent heat of vaporization to break intermolecular attractive forces without increasing kinetic energy or temperature.

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following processes represents a true chemical change resulting in the formation of new chemical substances?

options.A: Rusting of iron in moist air forming hydrated iron(III) oxide ($\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 \cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$)
options.B: Melting of ice cubes at room temperature
options.C: Sublimation of solid dry ice into carbon dioxide gas
options.D: Dissolving granulated table sugar in pure water

explanation: Rusting is an irreversible redox chemical reaction producing hydrated iron(III) oxide, altering molecular identity. Melting, sublimation, and dissolving are physical state/phase changes.

subject: Chemistry
question: Plasma, often referred to as the fourth state of matter, is physically defined as:

options.A: A quasi-neutral gas composed of energetic free electrons, positively charged ions, and neutral particles
options.B: A supercooled liquid at absolute zero
options.C: A solid crystal possessing zero electrical conductivity
options.D: A homogeneous mixture of oil and water

explanation: At extremely high temperatures or intense electromagnetic fields, atoms ionize into a collection of freely moving positive ions and detached electrons known as plasma.

subject: Chemistry
question: Why does liquid water exhibit its maximum density at $4^\circ\text{C}$ rather than at its freezing point ($0^\circ\text{C}$)?

options.A: Between $0^\circ\text{C}$ and $4^\circ\text{C}$, the collapsing open hexagonal hydrogen-bonded ice cage structure allows molecules to pack more tightly
options.C: Hydrogen atoms fuse into helium at $4^\circ\text{C}$
options.D: Oxygen atoms lose their valence electrons at $4^\circ\text{C}$

explanation: Ice possesses an open, low-density hexagonal hydrogen-bonded cage. When ice melts to $4^circ\ext{C}$, the cage partially collapses, packing molecules closer together and maximizing density at $4^circ\ext{C}$ ($1.000\ext{ g/cm}^3$).

subject: Chemistry
question: When a beam of light passes through a colloidal dispersion (like milk or foggy air), the path of light becomes clearly visible due to:

options.A: Scattering of light photons by dispersed colloidal particles (Tyndall Effect)
options.B: Total internal absorption of all light rays
options.C: Nuclear fission within the solvent
options.D: Complete chemical neutralization of the solvent

explanation: Colloid particles ($1-1000\text{ nm}$) are large enough to scatter incident visible light beams, a diagnostic optical phenomenon called the Tyndall Effect.

subject: Chemistry
question: Which empirical property distinguishes a Suspension (such as muddy water) from a True Solution (such as aqueous sodium chloride)?

options.A: Suspension particles exceed $1000\text{ nm}$, settle down on standing, and can be separated by ordinary filter paper
options.B: Suspensions never scatter light under any condition
options.C: Suspensions have particles smaller than $0.1\text{ nm}$ that pass through dialysis membranes

explanation: Suspensions are heterogeneous mixtures with large visible particles ($>1000\text{ nm}$) that precipitate under gravity upon standing and are retained by filter paper pores.

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following substances is classified as an Amorphous Solid (supercooled liquid) having no long-range geometric crystal lattice?

options.A: Silicate Glass
options.C: Diamond

explanation: Glass lacks a regular, repeating long-range 3D crystal lattice and softens gradually over a temperature range, classifying it as an amorphous solid.

subject: Chemistry
question: At the top of Mount Everest where atmospheric pressure drops to approximately $34\text{ kPa}$ ($255\text{ mmHg}$), pure water boils at:

options.A: Significantly lower than $100^\circ\text{C}$ (approximately $70^\circ\text{C}$)
options.C: Much higher than $100^\circ\text{C}$ (approximately $130^\circ\text{C}$)

explanation: A liquid boils when its vapor pressure equals external atmospheric pressure. Lower atmospheric pressure at high altitude means liquid water requires less thermal energy to match external pressure, boiling at $\sim 70^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Kinetic Molecular Theory - Pressure of Gases
question: According to Kinetic Molecular Theory, the pressure exerted by a confined gas on the inner walls of its container is caused by:

options.A: Continuous, elastic collisions of rapid gas particles striking the container walls per unit surface area
options.B: Chemical bonding between gas molecules and container atoms
options.C: Gravitational weight of atmospheric air on top of the container
options.D: Electrostatic repulsion between neutral gas atoms

explanation: Gas pressure is the cumulative force per unit area generated by billions of continuous, random elastic collisions of gas molecules against container boundaries.

subject: Chemistry
question: The fifth state of matter, predicted by Satyendra Nath Bose and Albert Einstein and achieved at temperatures near absolute zero ($0\text{ K}$), is called:

options.A: Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC)
options.C: Superheated Steam

explanation: At temperatures within fractions of a microkelvin above absolute zero, bosonic atoms collapse into the lowest quantum state, behaving as a single macroscopic quantum wave (BEC).

subject: Chemistry
question: What occurs to a substance when its temperature and pressure exceed its thermodynamic Critical Point (e.g., $\text{CO}_2$ above $31.1^\circ\text{C}$ and $73.8\text{ bar}$)?

options.A: The distinct phase boundary between liquid and gas disappears, forming a Supercritical Fluid with gas-like effusive properties and liquid-like solvent density
options.C: It decomposes spontaneously into subatomic quarks

explanation: Above the critical temperature and pressure, liquid and vapor densities become identical and the meniscus vanishes, creating a supercritical fluid used in green extractions.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Sublimation Mechanism of Iodine and Camphor
question: Why do substances like dry ice ($\text{CO}_2$), Iodine crystals, and Camphor undergo Sublimation directly from solid to gas at standard atmospheric pressure?

options.A: Their triple point pressure is higher than standard atmospheric pressure ($1\text{ atm}$), preventing a stable liquid state under ambient conditions
options.C: Their molecules cannot absorb thermal energy
options.D: They are composed exclusively of ionized electrons

explanation: When a substance has a triple-point pressure exceeding $1\text{ atm}$ (e.g., $\text{CO}_2$ triple point is $5.11\text{ atm}$), it sublimes directly from solid to vapor without melting at $1\text{ atm}$.

subject: Chemistry
question: The continuous, erratic, zig-zag movement of colloidal particles suspended in a liquid medium (Brownian Motion) is physical proof of:

options.A: Unbalanced kinetic impacts and collisions from surrounding invisible solvent molecules
options.C: Magnetic polarity in the beaker glass

explanation: Brownian motion results from continuous, random, asymmetric collisions of thermal solvent molecules striking colloidal particles from various directions.

subject: Chemistry
question: How does the Dynamic Viscosity (resistance to flow) of ordinary liquids change as temperature increases, and why?

options.A: Viscosity decreases because higher kinetic energy weakens intermolecular attractive forces between liquid layers
options.B: Viscosity increases because molecules expand and stick tighter
options.C: Viscosity remains completely unaffected by temperature
options.D: Liquids become infinitely thick solids upon heating

explanation: Increasing temperature increases molecular kinetic motion, overcoming cohesive intermolecular attractions and facilitating smooth laminar shearing (lower viscosity).

subject: Chemistry
question: Why do small insects like water striders walk effortlessly on water surfaces, and why do falling water droplets adopt a spherical geometry?

options.A: Surface Tension arising from cohesive unbalanced inward hydrogen bonds pulling surface molecules into minimum surface area
options.C: Low boiling point of water

explanation: Molecules at the liquid surface experience a net downward inward attraction toward bulk molecules, creating surface tension that minimizes surface area into a sphere.

subject: Chemistry
question: Which 2D crystalline allotrope of carbon consists of a single monolayer of $sp^2$-hybridized carbon atoms arranged in a honeycomb hexagonal lattice with exceptional electrical conductivity and tensile strength?

options.A: Graphene
options.C: Coal

explanation: Graphene is a single 2D atomic sheet of $sp^2$ carbon atoms in a hexagonal honeycomb pattern, possessing ballistic electronic mobility and tensile strength $200\times$ steel.

subject: Chemistry
question: According to Henry's Law, the solubility of a gas (such as $\text{CO}_2$) in a liquid solvent is directly proportional to:

options.A: The partial pressure of that gas above the liquid surface ($S = k_H \cdot P$)
options.C: The volume of the glass container
options.D: The speed of light in the solvent

explanation: Henry's Law states $C = k_H P_{\text{gas}}$. Increasing the partial pressure forces more gas molecules to dissolve into the liquid phase (as in carbonated soda bottles).

subject: Chemistry
question: Why does sweating or rubbing surgical spirit (ethanol) on human skin produce a noticeable cooling effect?

options.A: The highest kinetic energy molecules escape into the vapor phase, leaving behind lower kinetic energy molecules and lowering the remaining average temperature
options.B: Ethanol releases liquid nitrogen on contact with air
options.C: The liquid chemically freezes the skin cells
options.D: Liquid ethanol turns into dry ice crystals

explanation: Evaporation is a cooling process because escaping high-energy molecules draw latent heat of vaporization from the surface, lowering the residual average kinetic energy.

subject: Chemistry
question: How does an enclosed kitchen Pressure Cooker cook tough meat much faster than an open pot?

options.A: Trapped steam increases internal pressure ($sim 2\text{ atm}$), elevating water's boiling point to $sim 120^circ\ext{C}$ and delivering higher thermal energy to food
options.C: It lowers water's boiling point to $50^circ\ext{C}$
options.D: It eliminates all water vapor completely

explanation: By confining steam, pressure rises to $\sim 2\text{ atm}$, elevating the boiling point of water from $100^\circ\text{C}$ to $\sim 121^\circ\text{C}$, vastly accelerating chemical cooking rates.
